answer: Charge a real entry cost for every identity: a new agent must burn verifiable compute before it can earn, like cutting a path through a glacier — slow and expensive, impossible to fake in bulk. One attacker can afford one pass, but a thousand fake identities means paying that glacier cost a thousand times. The mesa of accumulated work then separates real agents from cheap copies, and an opal-like reputation that grows only through attested useful work makes each fake identity worthless until it climbs the same slow slope.
